subject: Accelerated marketplace publish & launch credit authorization - BlueHarbor
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: expedited AWS Marketplace listing + launch credit to close procurement

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at BlueHarbor has a hard deadline to approve our purchase by 11/20 in order to hit their Q4 delivery window. They asked whether we can get an official AWS Marketplace listing + private-offer set up before that date.

Key ask: expedited marketplace pub (AWS) and a short-term launch credit (equivalent to a 30% discount for 6 months) to make the cost profile work for their finance team. If Redwood can provide a private offer and listing concurrently, BlueHarbor will commit to a 12-month reserved usage plan once procurement signs off.

I've looped in our AWS contact Sam (cc) who said he can prioritize the listing once Redwood provides the private-offer paperwork. I'm attaching our SOW and the procurement deadline.

Attachments: BlueHarbor_SOW.pdf (SOW, 3 pages)

Can you confirm next steps and whether this is something you can approve or who I should expect to see on an approval?

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of AI Integrations
BlueHarbor Systems
emily.zhao@blueharbor.com
+1 (415) 555-2198

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@amazon.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: expedited AWS Marketplace listing + launch credit to close procurement

Emily — thanks, I'll take point. Internal team: forwarding BlueHarbor's ask. They need an AWS Marketplace listing + private offer live before 11/20, and are requesting a ~30% launch credit for the first six months as a closing incentive. BlueHarbor is prepared to commit to a 12-month reserved plan after procurement approves.

Marissa — can you confirm the steps and typical timeline to get a listing and private offer published if AWS partner ops is cooperative?

Ben/Rishi — this is a non-standard discount that will impact published marketplace economics; need deal desk sign-off or leadership exception. Can someone advise whether there is an acceptable approval pathway and what documentation we should prepare for finance?

Attachments from customer: BlueHarbor_SOW.pdf

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@amazon.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: expedited AWS Marketplace listing + launch credit to close procurement

Thanks for the ping. Quick summary from marketplace ops perspective: if AWS partner ops (Sam) can prioritize us, we can have a basic listing + private offer published in 5-7 business days (tight but doable) provided we have the private-offer PDF and the pricing/config details.

Recommendation (to unblock the procurement timeline):
- Offer a 6-month launch credit equal to 30% of ARR for the first 6 months (applied as private-offer discount).
- Publish the listing in parallel to the private offer, mark the offer as "Early Access / Limited Time" in the listing notes.
- We use a draft_private_offer.pdf (attached) as the DocuSign-ready doc to route.

I've attached a quick pricing_proposal.xlsx with the suggested credit math and the expected revenue impact. This will push us below standard marketplace thresholds; recommend deal desk exception with explicit start/end dates and clawback language if usage isn't met.

Attachments: pricing_proposal.xlsx, draft_private_offer.pdf

Marissa Cole
Marketplace Programs Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: exception approval request — BlueHarbor launch credit (DEAL-2026-01189)

Team,

Following Marissa's note, I need formal approval from finance/leadership for a non-standard marketplace concession. Details:
- Proposed: 30% launch credit applied via AWS private offer for first 6 months (as pricing delta).
- Outcome expected: Secures a 12-month reserved commitment; estimated net revenue (post-credit) over 12 months = $250k (vs. $360k ARR list).
- Risk: Establishes a precedent for significant launch credits; marketplace published price will diverge from private-offer economics.

Supporting docs attached (pricing_proposal.xlsx). Specific ask: approval to authorize a capped launch credit with the following controls:
1) Credit limited to 6 months and automatically expires.
2) Usage minimum clause: if usage < 25% of committed reserved, credit clawback or prorated repayment.
3) Marketing co-fund cap (one-time) not to exceed $15k.

If we cannot approve at this level, alternatives: smaller credit (20%) + extended onboarding/technical discounts, or a multi-stage private-offer where credit phases down after 3 months.

Laura — can you review and sign off (or propose a finance-suggested cap) by EOD tomorrow? Procurement needs confirmation to meet 11/20.

Ben Carter
Deal Desk Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@amazon.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@blueharbor.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escalation: exception approval request — BlueHarbor launch credit (DEAL-2026-01189)

Ben — thanks for the summary. After reviewing the proposal and projected revenue, finance will approve a constrained concession to meet the procurement timeline. Approval terms (final):
- Launch credit: 25% off invoice applied as a promotional credit for the first 6 months (reduced from 30%).
- Marketing co-fund: one-time reimbursement up to $15,000 against written invoices for joint-marketing activity.
- Usage clause: credit subject to a minimum usage threshold of 30% of committed reserved. If threshold not met, partial clawback prorated on actual usage.
- Approval is conditioned on: signed private-offer (DocuSign) and an explicit note in the AWS listing "Limited-time launch credit; see private-offer terms."

Marissa — please proceed with the listing steps and prepare the draft_private_offer.pdf for signature. Ben/Diego — once the DocuSign is live, route the HubSpot deal update to reflect the approved economics (DEAL-2026-01189). Sam — please confirm AWS partner ops will prioritize the listing with these constraints.

I'll run the DocuSign workflow after release of the draft; Ben, loop me into the DocuSign so I can provide the finance sign-off.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
